NEC partners test Wi-Fi HaLow tractor control over one kilometer

The Tokachi trial used 850 MHz connectivity for continuous video and simulated yam cultivation.

NEC Networks & System Integration / PR TIMES ↗29 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2

A large-field trial

JA Obihiro Kawanishi, NEC, NEC Networks & System Integration and Morse Micro disclosed a trial with a Yanmar robotic tractor in Tokachi, Hokkaido. It used 850 MHz Wi-Fi HaLow for remote monitoring and control up to 1,000 meters, alongside autonomous operation in simulated yam cultivation.

Continuous video over distance

The team used MM8108-EKH01 evaluation hardware to measure throughput against range and installed it on the tractor. The tested 850 MHz band avoids Japanese transmission-time constraints associated with 920 MHz. Participants reported no range shortfall or video-delay problem that disrupted this trial.

Multi-vehicle work remains ahead

Next steps include considering simultaneous tractors and AI-based work monitoring. This site-specific result is not a one-kilometer guarantee in every environment. Detailed latency and throughput figures were not provided, and the same spectrum arrangements do not automatically apply in other countries.
